description: The pie chart, titled in context as part of the paper “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media sources cited or analyzed within the study, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet and its relative frequency or weight in the dataset. The chart contains 18 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media organization and a numerical value indicating its share—presumably percentage points—of the total. The largest segment, colored blue, is “Breitbart” at 14%, followed by a gray “Other” category at 13%. “Drudge Report” and “The Daily Caller” each account for 8%, shown in orange and green respectively. “The Huffington Post” (7%, red), “NPR” and “Vox” (both 6%, purple and brown), and “The Guardian” and “BBC” (both 5%, pink and gray) follow in descending order. Smaller segments include “RT” (4%, yellow), “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Daily Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” and “CNN” (all 3%, in varying colors), and “Shareblue” and “PoliticoUSA” (both 3%, magenta and light pink). The slices are arranged radially around the center, with no apparent ordering by size, and each is labeled with its name and value directly adjacent to or inside the slice. A legend is not present; instead, labels are embedded within or near each segment, allowing direct identification. The visual design emphasizes relative proportions through slice area and color differentiation, facilitating quick comparison across media sources.
